concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 2 – Regime‑Switching VAR Estimation (FR‑004, SC‑004, SC‑005)
concerns.text: The plan proposes a Wald test (or bootstrap difference test) to assess lag‑1 autocorrelation differences across regimes (SC‑004) but does not specify a robust, fully bootstrap‑based procedure. Wald tests rely on asymptotic normality which may be unreliable with only ~1 800 observations per regime, risking inflated Type I error.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 2 – Regime‑Switching VAR Estimation (FR‑004, SC‑004, SC‑005)
concerns.text: No explicit stationarity check (e.g., ADF test) is performed on the log‑return series within each identified regime before fitting the VAR. Violations of stationarity would bias VAR coefficient estimates and undermine construct validity of the serial‑correlation measures.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 3 – Baseline VAR & Model Comparison (FR‑005, SC‑003, SC‑006)
concerns.text: The plan conducts multiple hypothesis tests (LR tests for regime distinctness, autocorrelation differences, cross‑asset correlation differences, BIC comparisons) but does not address multiple‑testing correction. Without adjustment, the overall false‑positive rate may exceed the nominal α = 0.05.

The sample size (~1 800 daily observations per asset) is assumed sufficient, yet no power analysis is provided to justify that the bootstrap LR tests and autocorrelation difference tests have adequate power to detect the effect sizes of interest.
